name: Cranial Neuralgia

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: International Classification of Headache Disorders (ICHD-3) Criteria for Cranial Neuralgia

criteria.description: Recurrent paroxysmal attacks of severe, sharp, stabbing pain in the distribution of one or more cranial nerves
Pain triggered by innocuous stimuli or specific trigger zones in the affected cranial nerve distribution
Absence of neurological deficit other than sensory abnormalities in the affected nerve territory
Pain relief with carbamazepine or other anticonvulsants supports diagnosis

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: At least two major criteria including paroxysmal pain and trigger points, plus absence of neurological deficit
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is clinical; imaging is used to exclude secondary causes.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Paroxysmal lancinating pain in cranial nerve distribution
Pain triggered by light touch or movement in trigger zones
searchTerms: pain triggered by touch or movement

common.symptomName: Unilateral facial pain localized to trigeminal nerve branches
Brief episodes lasting seconds to minutes
Sensory abnormalities such as numbness or tingling in affected nerve territory
Pain exacerbated by chewing or talking

occasional.symptomName: Muscle spasms or twitching in affected facial muscles
Headache localized to affected cranial nerve region
Autonomic symptoms such as lacrimation or nasal congestion
Mild facial weakness in severe cases

searchTerms: symptoms on both sides of face

rare.symptomName: Hearing loss associated with glossopharyngeal neuralgia
searchTerms: decreased hearing linked to nerve pain

rare.symptomName: Dysphagia or hoarseness due to vagus nerve involvement

imaging: MRI to exclude structural lesions compressing cranial nerves
other: Positive response to carbamazepine or oxcarbazepine
Trigger zone identification on clinical examination

distinguishingFeatures: Pain localized specifically to trigeminal nerve branches
Severe unilateral orbital pain with autonomic symptoms

redFlags: Signs of infection or systemic illness
references: International Classification of Headache Disorders, 3rd edition (ICHD-3), 2018
Cruccu G, et al. EFNS guidelines on trigeminal neuralgia management. Eur J Neurol. 2008
Zakrzewska JM, et al. Diagnosis and treatment of trigeminal neuralgia. BMJ. 2017
